title: Rejecting bad input with binding tags
summary: Binding tags on a ShouldBindJSON request, and a required int that turns away zero.

turns.user: create user accepts an empty name and garbage emails. reject those. age comes in negative sometimes too

assistant.body: Sure! ShouldBindJSON runs the validator over the binding tags, so adding tags to the struct is enough. The existing 400 branch already handles the failure. Age gets required plus a range, so anything from 0 to 130 works as expected.

turns.user: sent age 0 and got a 400. parents create accounts for their kids so 0 is a normal value here

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. On an int, required treats the zero value as missing, so 0 is rejected. With *int, required only checks for nil, and gte and lte apply to the value behind the pointer. In other words, leaving the field out and sending 0 are now two different things.

turns.user: also 50 chars for name is too short apparently. make it 100. no wait, product says 80

assistant.body: Note: max counts runes, not bytes, so a Japanese name also gets the full 80 characters. Only the number in the tag changes.
